messages:
Sam: Quick thread — we need a short, operational playbook for pilot candidate acceptance + declines. Current problem: ~25% of accepted pilots drop before kickoff. Goal: <10% drop. Can we align on commit window, reminder cadence, decline handling, and a fallback list?
Maya: I can draft. proposal: 72-hour hold for acceptance, automatic reminder at 48h and 12h, and an opt-in backup list for waitlist. if they decline we move to waitlist immediately.
Ilana: From infra: we need a 7-day engineering buffer between confirmed cohort and kickoff to allocate capacity + onboarding work. If someone declines within that 7-day buffer, we can’t always reassign their slot unless waitlist candidate passes a short checklist.
Chris: CSM perspective — we lose signal if the candidate never schedules the onboarding call. add a mandatory 15-min scheduling step in the acceptance flow (Calendly link) and mark anyone who doesn’t schedule within 72h as "at risk" for follow-up.
Jorge: Design note: acceptance language matters. Keep the initial email short, highlight commitment steps, and mention incentive clearly. draft email below: 

```
Subject: You're in — Pilot slot confirmation and next steps
Hi [Name],
Thanks for joining our pilot cohort. To secure your slot please: 1) Confirm within 72 hours, 2) Book the 30-min onboarding call here: [calendly link], 3) Complete the 5-min pre-kickoff survey.
We’ll hold your slot for 72 hours; if you decline or don’t confirm we’ll offer it to the next person on the waitlist. You’ll receive $200 credit after successful completion of the pilot.
Cheers,
Product Team
```

Maya: +1. Add explicit decline flow copy: if they decline, ask optional reason (single-select) and offer to join waitlist. capture reason metric.
Sam: What about no-shows? if they confirm but don’t show to onboarding call within the buffer window?
Chris: No-show policy: after two missed scheduling/contact attempts we mark the slot as open and pull from waitlist. But first reach-outs should be human: 1) automated email, 2) CSM Slack/LinkedIn if provided.
Ilana: We also need a small technical gating checklist for waitlist swaps so we don’t lose time. example: repo access, test dataset availability, account credentials. we can make it a 3-point checklist in the intake form.
recruit-bot: Automated messages ready: 
- 48h reminder: "Your pilot slot is waiting. Confirm + schedule onboarding: [link]"
- 12h reminder: "Final reminder to confirm your pilot slot — it will be released in 12 hours if not confirmed."
- Decline follow-up: "Sorry to hear you can’t make it — would you like to join the waitlist? (Yes / No)"

Maya: Metrics to track (KPI): acceptance -> scheduled (target 90%), scheduled -> attended onboarding (target 95%), acceptance -> final completion (target 75%), decline reasons (categorical). also measure time-to-fill from decline to replacement (target <72h).
Sam: Can we add a short SLA for waitlist replacements? Ideally 48-72h to confirm replacement. Also flag if replacement requires infra changes (Ilana) we may need extra lead time.
Ilana: Agree. Flag replacements that require infra work and route them to eng on-call. Add boolean field in intake: "requires infra allocation" so we can triage fast.
Chris: Handoff template to CSM on confirmed slot: 
- Candidate name, org, contact, use-case summary (1-2 lines), kickoff availability, intake checklist status, incentive agreed.

Maya: I'll prototype the acceptance + decline copy and the intake + scheduling form today. Sam — can you own the rollout checklist and final sign-off?
Sam: Yep. I'll compile the playbook and share a one-pager we can use in recruitment threads. Goal: ship this operationally in 1 week.
Jorge: I’ll review copy + incentive phrasing.
Chris: I’ll set up the Calendly template + CSM routing.
Sam: Great — next steps: Maya to post draft by EOD, then 24h review window. If all good, we enable the automated reminders and start a compact cohort next week. :rocket:
